The rider required [COMPANY_A] to pay for testing the air and covered property to determine the presence or level of mold and, if mold was present, to pay for its removal, including tearing out property needed to access it. On October 5, 2007, after [PERSON_A] and [PERSON_B] moved into the property, [PERSON_A], assisted by a contractor, began renovating the basement and removed part of the wood paneling covering the basement’s block walls. After the paneling was detached, [PERSON_A] discovered two areas of black mold on the block walls near leaking water pipes. [PERSON_A] informed [COMPANY_A] and said he wished to initiate a claim under the homeowner’s policy. [COMPANY_A] sent an adjuster to view the mold, and two days later the adjuster returned with an engineer employed by [COMPANY_B], which [COMPANY_A] had retained to investigate the mold, determine its severity, and assess the extent of remediation required. The complaint alleged that, after [PERSON_A] requested payment to have the mold tested, [COMPANY_A]’s adjuster and [COMPANY_B]’s engineer told him that the mold was harmless, that he and [PERSON_B] should continue removing the paneling, and that health problems associated with mold were exaggerated. The adjuster refused payment, stating that he lacked authorization and that no coverage determination had been made. Based on the adjuster’s and engineer’s assurances that the mold was not a health hazard, [PERSON_A] and [PERSON_B] continued living in the property, and [PERSON_A] continued renovating it. During October, [PERSON_A] and a contractor attempted to eradicate the mold and removed additional paneling, revealing more leaking pipes and additional mold. [PERSON_A] informed [COMPANY_A] of the further discoveries. [COMPANY_A] sent the same engineer, who visually inspected the newly discovered mold and performed tests but did not disclose the results. The engineer and adjuster allegedly did not inform [PERSON_A] and [PERSON_B] of the mold’s health hazard or indicate that it should be removed or remediated. During October, each family member began experiencing respiratory ailments that worsened over the following months. By January 2008, [PERSON_B] had developed severe coughing, difficulty breathing and clearing her throat, and intense headaches. [PERSON_A] and [PERSON_B] then paid for mold testing, which revealed that the mold was toxic and hazardous to human health. In April 2008, [COMPANY_A] paid [PERSON_A] and [PERSON_B] [CURRENCY_AMOUNT_A] under the mold endorsement. [PERSON_B] was later diagnosed with throat and esophageal cancer, which her treating physicians attributed to exposure to toxic mold. [PERSON_A] and [PERSON_B] later left the property, which they subsequently demolished because the mold could not be eradicated. [PERSON_A] and [PERSON_B] alleged that the adjuster’s and engineer’s advice caused them to continue removing basement paneling, which led to health problems from mold exposure and caused the property to become uninhabitable and require destruction. The parties agreed that [COMPANY_A] paid [PERSON_A] and [PERSON_B] [CURRENCY_AMOUNT_A] for testing and remediation of property damage. neutral_fact_source: In September 2007, [PERSON_A] and [PERSON_B] purchased a home from [PERSON_E] and [PERSON_F] and obtained a homeowner’s insurance policy for it from [COMPANY_A]. The policy covered [PERSON_A] and [PERSON_B] and their two minor children, [PERSON_C] and [PERSON_D], and included an endorsement covering physical loss to the property caused by mold. The rider obligated [COMPANY_A] to pay the Brunos up to [CURRENCY_AMOUNT_A] for direct physical loss to the property caused by mold or necessary increased costs. The rider required [COMPANY_A] to pay for testing the air and covered property to determine the presence or level of mold and, if mold was present, to pay for its removal, including tearing out property needed to access it. On October 5, 2007, after [PERSON_A] and [PERSON_B] moved into the property, [PERSON_A], assisted by a contractor, began renovating the basement and removed part of the wood paneling covering the basement’s block walls. After the paneling was detached, [PERSON_A] discovered two areas of black mold on the block walls near leaking water pipes. [PERSON_A] informed [COMPANY_A] and said he wished to initiate a claim under the homeowner’s policy. [COMPANY_A] sent an adjuster to view the mold, and two days later the adjuster returned with an engineer employed by [COMPANY_B], which [COMPANY_A] had retained to investigate the mold, determine its severity, and assess the extent of remediation required. The complaint alleged that, after [PERSON_A] requested payment to have the mold tested, [COMPANY_A]’s adjuster and [COMPANY_B]’s engineer told him that the mold was harmless, that he and [PERSON_B] should continue removing the paneling, and that health problems associated with mold were exaggerated. The adjuster refused payment, stating that he lacked authorization and that no coverage determination had been made. Based on the adjuster’s and engineer’s assurances that the mold was not a health hazard, [PERSON_A] and [PERSON_B] continued living in the property, and [PERSON_A] continued renovating it. During October, [PERSON_A] and a contractor attempted to eradicate the mold and removed additional paneling, revealing more leaking pipes and additional mold. [PERSON_A] informed [COMPANY_A] of the further discoveries. [COMPANY_A] sent the same engineer, who visually inspected the newly discovered mold and performed tests but did not disclose the results. The engineer and adjuster allegedly did not inform [PERSON_A] and [PERSON_B] of the mold’s health hazard or indicate that it should be removed or remediated. During October, each family member began experiencing respiratory ailments that worsened over the following months. By January 2008, [PERSON_B] had developed severe coughing, difficulty breathing and clearing her throat, and intense headaches. [PERSON_A] and [PERSON_B] then paid for mold testing, which revealed that the mold was toxic and hazardous to human health. In April 2008, [COMPANY_A] paid [PERSON_A] and [PERSON_B] [CURRENCY_AMOUNT_A] under the mold endorsement. [PERSON_B] was later diagnosed with throat and esophageal cancer, which her treating physicians attributed to exposure to toxic mold. [PERSON_A] and [PERSON_B] later left the property, which they subsequently demolished because the mold could not be eradicated. [PERSON_A] and [PERSON_B] alleged that the adjuster’s and engineer’s advice caused them to continue removing basement paneling, which led to health problems from mold exposure and caused the property to become uninhabitable and require destruction. The parties agreed that [COMPANY_A] paid [PERSON_A] and [PERSON_B] [CURRENCY_AMOUNT_A] for testing and remediation of property damage. [COMPANY_A] asserted that its adjuster and [COMPANY_B]’s engineer were in the property only because of the insurance relationship and assessed water damage and mold only to process [PERSON_A] and [PERSON_B]’s benefits claim. According to the complaint, [PERSON_A] and [PERSON_B] did not engage, employ, or retain [COMPANY_B] to provide engineering services to them. [COMPANY_A] retained [COMPANY_B] to provide engineering services to [COMPANY_A] to evaluate mold damage to the property.

neutral_fact_en: [PERSON_A] worked as a groundskeeper and golf course superintendent for nearly forty years. His work involved regularly applying [PRODUCT_GROUP_A], primarily insecticides and fungicides. During this period, [PERSON_A] kept a detailed record of the products used and their application dates. [PERSON_B], a coworker, testified about how [PERSON_A] applied the pesticides, the products and concentrations used, and the protective gear they wore. Initially, they used only gloves; later, they also used overalls, rubber boots, masks, and eventually disposable protective gear. [PERSON_B] explained that, despite the protective gear, [PERSON_A] was exposed to dust from the pesticide products while opening bags and mixing chemicals. On October 5, 2008, [PERSON_A] arrived at an emergency room with fever, chills, and a cough. A bone marrow biopsy resulted in a diagnosis of Acute Myelogenous Leukemia (AML). Cytogenetic testing revealed significant chromosomal aberrations. [PERSON_A] died on February 2, 2009. [PERSON_C] later opined that [PERSON_A]’s extensive exposure to pesticides raised a high degree of suspicion that the exposure played a significant role in the development of [PERSON_A]’s AML. [PERSON_A]’s executor brought claims against [COMPANY_GROUP_A], whose products [PERSON_A] had applied during his career. The remaining manufacturers made fifteen pesticide products to which [PERSON_A] was exposed. [PERSON_A] developed AML, had significant chromosomal aberrations identified through cytogenetic testing, and died on February 2, 2009. [PERSON_A]’s expert identified studies stating that the active ingredients in the specific pesticides were genotoxic and caused chromosomal abnormalities. The expert further stated that pesticide or benzene exposure causing AML is associated with abnormalities of the fifth and seventh chromosomes, which initiate a carcinogenic process, and that this pattern was identified in [PERSON_A]’s cytogenetic testing. The expert conducted product-specific analyses of each [PRODUCT_GROUP_A], evaluated the chemical components individually, and concluded that each product contained chemicals that were genotoxic or caused DNA damage and were therefore carcinogenic. The expert concluded that exposure to organophosphate pesticide formulations, individually or in combination, was causally related to an increased risk of leukemia in exposed humans.
neutral_fact_ko: [PERSON_A]는 거의 40년 동안 코스 관리원 및 골프장 관리자로 일했다. [PERSON_A]의 업무에는 [PRODUCT_GROUP_A], 주로 살충제와 살균제를 정기적으로 살포하는 일이 포함되었다. 이 기간 동안 [PERSON_A]는 사용한 제품과 그 살포 날짜를 상세히 기록했다. 동료인 [PERSON_B]는 [PERSON_A]가 살충제를 어떻게 살포했는지, 사용한 제품과 농도, 그리고 그들이 착용한 보호 장비에 대해 증언했다. 처음에는 그들은 장갑만 사용했지만, 나중에는 작업복, 고무 장화, 마스크, 그리고 결국 일회용 보호 장비도 사용했다. [PERSON_B]는 보호 장비에도 불구하고 [PERSON_A]가 봉지를 열고 화학물질을 혼합하는 동안 살충제 제품에서 나온 먼지에 노출되었다고 설명했다. 2008년 10월 5일, [PERSON_A]는 발열, 오한 및 기침 증상으로 응급실에 도착했다. 골수 생검 결과 급성 골수성 백혈병(AML) 진단을 받았다. 세포유전학적 검사에서 상당한 염색체 이상이 확인되었다. [PERSON_A]는 2009년 2월 2일 사망했다. [PERSON_C]는 나중에 [PERSON_A]의 광범위한 살충제 노출로 인해 그 노출이 [PERSON_A]의 AML 발병에 중요한 역할을 했다는 강한 의심이 제기된다는 의견을 밝혔다. [PERSON_A]의 유언집행자는 [PERSON_A]가 경력期间 사용했던 제품을 제조한 [COMPANY_GROUP_A]를 상대로 주장을 제기했다. 나머지 제조업체들은 [PERSON_A]가 노출된 살충제 제품 15개를 제조했다. [PERSON_A]는 AML이 발병했고, 세포유전학적 검사를 통해 상당한 염색체 이상이 확인되었으며, 2009년 2월 2일 사망했다. [PERSON_A]의 전문가는 특정 살충제의 유효성분이 유전독성이 있고 염색체 이상을 유발한다고 밝힌 연구들을 제시했다. 전문가는 또한 AML을 유발하는 살충제 또는 벤젠 노출은 제5번 및 제7번 염색체의 이상과 관련되어 있으며, 이러한 이상이 발암 과정을 시작하고, 이 패턴이 [PERSON_A]의 세포유전학적 검사에서 확인되었다고 말했다. 전문가는 각 [PRODUCT_GROUP_A]에 대해 제품별 분석을 실시하고 화학 성분을 개별적으로 평가한 후, 각 제품에 유전독성이 있거나 DNA 손상을 유발하는 화학물질이 포함되어 있으며 따라서 발암성이라고 결론 내렸다. 전문가는 유기인계 살충제 제형에 개별적으로 또는 복합적으로 노출되는 것이 노출된 사람의 백혈병 위험 증가와 인과관계가 있다고 결론 내렸다.

neutral_fact_en: On November 6, 1998, [PERSON_A] was involved in a single-vehicle accident, was hospitalized at [INSTITUTION_A], and was transferred to [INSTITUTION_B] for rehabilitation therapy. The accident caused [PERSON_A] to suffer spinal cord injuries and paraplegia. While receiving rehabilitation therapy at [INSTITUTION_B], [PERSON_A] developed pressure wounds on the buttocks and sacrum. The pressure wounds became infected, requiring [PERSON_A] to return to [INSTITUTION_A] for surgical debridement and therapy. [PERSON_A] alleged that the nursing staff of [INSTITUTION_A] and [INSTITUTION_B] failed to meet the applicable nursing care requirements for treating and preventing pressure wounds in an immobilized patient. [ORGANIZATION_A] and [ORGANIZATION_B] maintained that the ulcer was neither avoidable nor related to the care [PERSON_A] received from them. [PERSON_A]'s amended complaint stated that malnutrition, metabolic abnormalities, bacteria, and inadequate repositioning may have caused or contributed to the ulcer's formation or progression.

neutral_fact_en: In 1993, [LOCAL_GOVERNMENT_A] constructed a public sewer system under a written contract with [COMPANY_A] and [FIRM_A]. Rebuilding [LOCATION_A] required work adjacent to the home of [PERSON_A] and [PERSON_B] and their children, [PERSON_C], [PERSON_D], and [PERSON_E]. During a one-week period of repeated heavy rains shortly after the rebuilding, the basement flooded three times. [PERSON_A] believed the rebuilt roadway's pitch drained excessive rainwater onto the property, contacted [LOCAL_GOVERNMENT_A], and [LOCAL_GOVERNMENT_A] installed a corrective swale after which the flooding ceased. In late summer 1997, [PERSON_A] and [PERSON_D] began renovating the basement, removed all interior walls and carpeting, and observed water-stained and moldy sheetrock, discolored insulation and building studs, and black, green, and white discoloration beneath the carpeting. Shortly after the walls and carpeting were removed, [PERSON_A] became ill and the renovation was not completed. Beginning in fall 1997, all members of the household repeatedly experienced physical ailments; [PERSON_A] had a chronic cough, shortness of breath, repeated vomiting, burning eyes, and fatigue, while [PERSON_B] developed uterine polyps, migraine headaches, and fungal infections on her fingernails and toenails. [PERSON_D] experienced recurrent cold symptoms, acne on his chest, face, and back, and sinus polyps requiring surgical removal. [PERSON_C] suffered recurrent nosebleeds and skin boils, and [PERSON_E] had frequent bronchitis and scaly, itchy skin. Physicians treated each family member from 1997 to 2000. In early 2000, [PERSON_A] watched a television program about a mold-contaminated home whose residents became ill with symptoms similar to those experienced by the household. [PERSON_A] and the other household members then retained counsel, who engaged [COMPANY_B] to test the air quality in [HOME_A]. The test occurred in March 2000, and [COMPANY_B] prepared a report dated April 10, 2000. The report showed that air throughout [HOME_A], particularly in the basement, contained fungal and bacterial organisms at counts vastly exceeding recommended safe levels. Several species were described as highly pathogenic and potentially life-threatening, and immediate corrective action was required. [PERSON_A], [PERSON_B], [PERSON_C], [PERSON_D], and [PERSON_E] abandoned [HOME_A] and most of its contents, including clothing and furniture, on June 1, 2000. [PERSON_A], [PERSON_B], [PERSON_C], [PERSON_D], and [PERSON_E] alleged that construction of the roadway and corrective swale caused rainwater runoff to accumulate, resulting in permanent moisture around the foundation of [HOME_A] that caused toxic mold to form. [PERSON_A] testified that, although the corrective swale installed by [LOCAL_GOVERNMENT_A] resolved the initial flooding, it did not prevent excess rainwater runoff from continuously seeping into the foundation of [HOME_A]. [PERSON_A] testified that he believed the problem had been solved when the swale was installed and learned only after a later investigation that the swale continued to permit excess rainwater to accumulate around the foundation of [HOME_A]. neutral_fact_source: [PERSON_A] and [PERSON_B] named [COMPANY_A], [ORGANIZATION_A], and [PERSON_C] as defendants in an action concerning [PERSON_A]’s medical care. In June 2013, [PERSON_A] found a lump in her right breast and underwent a mammogram. [PERSON_C] interpreted the mammogram, diagnosed the lump as “benign appearing cysts,” and recommended annual mammograms. In 2013, [PERSON_A] discovered the breast mass, brought it to her doctor’s attention, and continued monitoring it after receiving a mammogram report that did not show cancer. [PERSON_A] noticed that the mass persisted in 2014, sought additional testing, observed that it had increased in size in 2015, and brought her concerns to her physician to obtain further testing. In April 2015, a biopsy revealed “invasive ductal carcinoma with lobular features,” and in May 2015, a double mastectomy revealed that the cancer had spread to a lymph node. In July 2016, a biopsy revealed that the cancer had spread further, into [PERSON_A]’s bone marrow. The delayed diagnosis might have been caused by a misreading of the 2013 mammogram. In August 2016, [PERSON_A] sought a second opinion from a specialist, who told her that [PERSON_C] might have misread the 2013 mammogram. [PERSON_A] continued to follow up and was diagnosed in July 2016 with cancer in her bone marrow. [COMPANY_A] and [ORGANIZATION_A] alleged that [PERSON_A] would have discovered that the misread mammogram caused a delayed diagnosis after her diagnosis of metastatic breast cancer. [PERSON_A] did not learn that the underlying error from 2013 was a possible cause of her injury until August 2016.

neutral_fact_en: In April 1999, [PERSON_A] purchased a spray bottle of [PRODUCT_A] from [COMPANY_A]. [COMPANY_C], later acquired by [COMPANY_D], packaged and labeled [PRODUCT_A], a spray-on body and hair moisturizer containing eight natural oils. The label warned users not to spray the product near sparks or an open flame, but it did not state that the product could be harmful or fatal if swallowed or that it should be kept out of reach of children. [PERSON_A]'s 11-month-old son, [PERSON_B], was left unattended and obtained the bottle, which had been within his reach. He put an unknown amount of the product into his mouth, and some entered his lungs. He was admitted to a hospital with hydrocarbon ingestion and chemical pneumonitis and died about one month later from multisystem organ failure associated with chemical pneumonitis after hydrocarbon ingestion. [PERSON_A] stated that the bottle had been intact when she last used it earlier that day; when she later saw [PERSON_B] with the bottle, the plastic top and pump actuator were missing, and the plastic base of the pump actuator was cracked. [PERSON_A] also stated that she generally read product labels because she had two small children and kept products she knew to be toxic in locked storage.

[PERSON_A]의 11개월 된 아들 [PERSON_B]는 보호자 없이 있던 중 손이 닿는 곳에 있던 제품 병을 손에 넣었다. [PERSON_B]는 알 수 없는 양의 제품을 입에 넣었고 일부가 폐로 들어갔다. [PERSON_B]는 탄화수소 섭취와 화학성 폐렴으로 병원에 입원했고, 약 한 달 뒤 탄화수소 섭취에 따른 화학성 폐렴과 관련된 다기관 장기부전으로 사망했다. [PERSON_A]는 그날 앞서 제품을 마지막으로 사용했을 때 병이 온전했다고 진술했으나, 나중에 [PERSON_B]가 병을 들고 있는 것을 보았을 때 플라스틱 상단과 펌프 작동기가 없어져 있었고 펌프 작동기의 플라스틱 바닥 부분이 갈라져 있었다고 진술했다. [PERSON_A]는 어린 자녀가 둘 있어 일반적으로 제품 라벨을 읽었고, 유독하다고 알고 있는 제품은 잠금장치가 있는 곳에 보관했다고 진술했다.

neutral_fact_en: [PERSON_A] completed a three-week course provided by [ORGANIZATION_A] in which he was taught methods of climbing wooden utility poles. In February 1993, [PERSON_A] attended a three-week class provided by [ORGANIZATION_A] in which he was instructed regarding how to climb a wooden utility pole using equipment designed for that purpose. At the end of the course, [PERSON_A] purchased from [ORGANIZATION_A] the equipment that he had used during the course. This equipment consisted of a body belt, gaffs, and a pole strap. Shortly after completing the three-week climbing course, [PERSON_A] was hired by [COMPANY_A] as an apprentice linesman. On April 3, 1993, [PERSON_A] was working on a utility pole. While descending the pole, he fell to the ground from a height of approximately 18.3 meters. [PERSON_A] received serious injuries from the fall. At the time of the fall, [PERSON_A] had disconnected his pole strap to maneuver around a \"cross bar\" extending from the pole. The climbing method taught by [ORGANIZATION_A] involved unhooking the pole strap from the \"D\" ring on the body belt, moving past the obstacle, and rehooking the strap around the pole. [PERSON_A] alleged that [ORGANIZATION_A] supplied inappropriate climbing equipment and failed to provide adequate instructions, education, and warnings regarding pole climbing. [PERSON_A] testified that the manner in which he attempted to negotiate the obstacle was the only method taught to him by [ORGANIZATION_A]. [ORGANIZATION_A] argued that it had no responsibility to instruct [PERSON_A] to use fall arrest equipment. [PERSON_A] alleged that, while descending the utility pole with the equipment in the manner prescribed by [ORGANIZATION_A], he was injured while descending around the cross-arms, and that he would not have fallen but for [ORGANIZATION_A]'s improper instructions. [PERSON_A]'s expert testified that [PERSON_A] should have been instructed to use a second pole strap and that the second strap would have prevented the accident.
neutral_fact_ko: [PERSON_A]는 [ORGANIZATION_A]가 제공한 3주 과정의 교육을 이수했으며, 그 교육에서 목재 전신주를 오르는 방법을 배웠다. 1993년 2월, [PERSON_A]는 [ORGANIZATION_A]가 제공한 3주 수업에 참석했으며, 그 수업에서 해당 목적을 위해 설계된 장비를 사용하여 목재 전신주를 오르는 방법에 관한 교육을 받았다. 과정이 끝날 때 [PERSON_A]는 과정 중 사용했던 장비를 [ORGANIZATION_A]로부터 구입했다. 이 장비는 안전벨트, 가프 및 전주 스트랩으로 구성되어 있었다. 3주간의 등반 과정을 마친 직후, [PERSON_A]는 [COMPANY_A]에 견습 전선공으로 고용되었다. 1993년 4월 3일, [PERSON_A]는 전신주에서 작업하고 있었다. 전신주를 내려오던 중 그는 약 18.3미터 높이에서 지면으로 추락했다. [PERSON_A]는 추락으로 중상을 입었다. 추락 당시 [PERSON_A]는 전신주에서 뻗어 나온 "크로스 바"를 돌아 이동하기 위해 전주 스트랩을 분리한 상태였다. [ORGANIZATION_A]가 가르친 등반 방법은 안전벨트의 "D" 링에서 전주 스트랩의 고리를 풀고, 장애물을 지나 이동한 다음, 전신주 주위에 스트랩을 다시 거는 것이었다. [PERSON_A]는 [ORGANIZATION_A]가 부적절한 등반 장비를 제공했고 전신주 등반에 관한 적절한 지시, 교육 및 경고를 제공하지 않았다고 주장했다. [PERSON_A]는 자신이 장애물을 통과하려고 시도한 방식이 [ORGANIZATION_A]가 자신에게 가르친 유일한 방법이었다고 증언했다. [ORGANIZATION_A]는 [PERSON_A]에게 추락 방지 장비를 사용하도록 지시할 책임이 없다고 주장했다. [PERSON_A]는 [ORGANIZATION_A]가 정한 방식으로 장비를 착용하고 전신주를 내려오던 중 크로스암 주위를 내려오다가 부상을 입었으며, [ORGANIZATION_A]의 부적절한 지시가 없었다면 추락하지 않았을 것이라고 주장했다. [PERSON_A]의 전문가는 [PERSON_A]에게 두 번째 전주 스트랩을 사용하도록 지시했어야 하며, 두 번째 스트랩이 사고를 방지했을 것이라고 증언했다.

[PERSON_B] died from the injuries allegedly caused by being struck by the bus. The alleged push or fall from the sidewalk placed [PERSON_B] in the path of the oncoming bus, which allegedly struck her and caused the injuries from which she died. The bus carrying [PERSON_C] and [PERSON_D] stopped, and they were forced to exit it and saw [PERSON_B]'s injured body. The petition alleged that [PERSON_G] saw or should have seen the large student gathering and the fight between [PERSON_B] and [PERSON_E], yet continued operating the bus near the crowd without regard for the children's safety. The petition alleged that [PERSON_F]'s role in inciting the fight and [PERSON_E]'s alleged push of [PERSON_B], which allegedly caused her to fall, contributed to the resulting harm. neutral_fact_en: [PERSON_A] and [PERSON_B] pursued a claim against [COMPANY_A] after [PERSON_A], while employed by [COMPANY_B], fell at a [COMPANY_A] facility; their filing requested that [COMPANY_A] be served through [COMPANY_C], its process-service agent. [COMPANY_C] employees testified that bundles of service documents were delivered each morning, usually received and counted by the first employee to arrive, and recorded on a running tally. According to the office log, [PERSON_D] delivered 57 documents to [COMPANY_C] on November 1, 1995, and signed the service returns one or two days later to indicate that each document had been delivered. [PERSON_D] testified that process servers delivered documents to any employee who did not refuse to receive them, and that [COMPANY_C] later checked received bundles against a detailed log after the sheriff's office began sending such logs. [PERSON_D] did not know whether he delivered [PERSON_A] and [PERSON_B]'s original filing to [COMPANY_C] on November 1, 1995, and the recorded statement that he delivered it personally to [PERSON_C] was questioned.

[PERSON_C] argued that the harm would have occurred even if [PERSON_A] had been released to [PERSON_B], while the dissenting opinion characterized that proposition as speculation. neutral_fact_en: [PERSON_A] was a tenant at [PROPERTY_A], a complex owned by [COMPANY_A] and [COMPANY_B]. On June 25, 1999, after returning home from work, [PERSON_A] took [ANIMAL_A] for a walk around the apartment complex. During the walk, [PERSON_A] and [ANIMAL_A] traversed a sidewalk in a common area of the complex. The grass strip was approximately 3.35 meters wide and was elevated above the parking lot approximately 1.22 meters. The grass strip was supported laterally by a white brick retaining wall, and there was no fence or other structure along the edge of the retaining wall. As [PERSON_A] and [ANIMAL_A] walked along the sidewalk, a girl in a nearby apartment unexpectedly let [ANIMAL_B] out of her apartment. [ANIMAL_B] were larger than [ANIMAL_A], and they rushed toward [PERSON_A] and [ANIMAL_A] snarling and snapping. [PERSON_A] quickly retreated backwards to pull [ANIMAL_A] away from the attacking [ANIMAL_B]. [PERSON_A] moved off of the sidewalk and across the grass strip. In her haste, she backed up to the edge of the grass strip, stumbled over the edge of the retaining wall, and fell onto the parking lot below. After falling onto the parking lot below, [PERSON_A] suffered fractures to a rib, a hip, and a femur. The attacking [ANIMAL_B] caused [PERSON_A] to retreat across the grass strip; while retreating, [PERSON_A] stumbled over the edge of the retaining wall and fell onto the parking lot, resulting in fractures to a rib, a hip, and a femur. Construction of the retaining wall had been completed in 1987, and the retaining wall had remained structurally unchanged since that time. [COMPANY_A] and [COMPANY_B] were not the original owners of the apartment complex. [PERSON_A] alleged that [COMPANY_A] and [COMPANY_B] had failed to design, build, and maintain a reasonably safe retaining wall and had failed to warn her about the hazard. neutral_fact_en: In May 1991, [PERSON_A] and [PERSON_E] purchased a used [PRODUCT_A] from a dealership. In addition to gasoline propulsion engines, [PRODUCT_A] contained a small [PRODUCT_B] that powered its accessories, including the [PRODUCT_C]. On May 29, 1993, during a weekend cruise at [LOCATION_A], [PERSON_A] and [PERSON_B] secured [PRODUCT_A] alongside a beach, went to sleep in its cabin, and left [PRODUCT_B] running to power [PRODUCT_C]. The next morning, [PERSON_F], a friend staying at the beach, knocked on the cabin door and received no response; later that afternoon, [PERSON_F] boarded [PRODUCT_A] and found [PERSON_A] dead and [PERSON_B] barely breathing. [PERSON_F] testified that the engines were not running during either check, and a subsequent investigation identified [PRODUCT_B], rather than the engines, as the source of the carbon monoxide, which is tasteless and odorless. [PERSON_A] died and [PERSON_B] suffered catastrophic injuries from carbon monoxide poisoning during an overnight outing in [PRODUCT_A] at [LOCATION_A]. The injuries suffered by [PERSON_A] and [PERSON_B] were caused by odorless and tasteless carbon monoxide fumes from [PRODUCT_B], which powered [PRODUCT_C], rather than by exhaust fumes. Two warnings about carbon monoxide poisoning accompanied the sale of this type of [PRODUCT_A] in 1981: one was written by [ORGANIZATION_A], the generator manufacturer, and the other by [ORGANIZATION_B]. [COMPANY_A] also provided purchasers with other manuals. Both warnings primarily addressed carbon monoxide exposure from engine exhaust. When [PERSON_A] and [PERSON_E] purchased [PRODUCT_A], the dealership service manager, [PERSON_G], and salesperson, [PERSON_H], warned them about exhaust fumes and carbon monoxide and the need to ventilate [PRODUCT_A] to remove hazardous fumes. [PERSON_G] and [PERSON_H] demonstrated flow-through ventilation by opening a window and the hatch, explained that the rear door should remain open when the main propulsion engines were running, and [PERSON_G] stated that idling the engine with the front hatch closed could cause carbon monoxide to accumulate. [PERSON_B], [PERSON_C], and [PERSON_D] alleged that "migrating carbon monoxide" caused the incident when carbon monoxide safely exhausted from [PRODUCT_B] into the open air was blown back into [PRODUCT_A] by wind and entered the passenger cabin through small openings. [COMPANY_A]'s expert agreed with this causal explanation but testified that the phenomenon was rare and that ventilation in the passenger cabin had to be obstructed for carbon monoxide to accumulate to dangerous levels. The expert identified three precautions: posting a watch because carbon monoxide detection devices were unavailable in 1981; anchoring [PRODUCT_A] from the bow rather than the side so wind currents would blow away from the stern; or creating flow-through ventilation before sleeping. The expert conceded that [COMPANY_A]'s manual contained none of those instructions or warnings, but testified that no death-causing incident of that type had been reported for the particular [PRODUCT_A] model involved.
neutral_fact_ko: 1991년 5월, [PERSON_A]와 [PERSON_E]는 판매점에서 중고 [PRODUCT_A]를 구입했다. [PRODUCT_A]에는 가솔린 추진 엔진 외에도 [PRODUCT_C]를 포함한 부속 장치에 동력을 공급하는 소형 [PRODUCT_B]가 들어 있었다. 1993년 5월 29일, [LOCATION_A]에서 주말 항해를 하던 중 [PERSON_A]와 [PERSON_B]는 해변 옆에 [PRODUCT_A]를 계류하고 그 선실에서 잠들었으며, [PRODUCT_C]에 동력을 공급하기 위해 [PRODUCT_B]를 작동시킨 채로 두었다. 다음 날 아침, 해변에 머물고 있던 친구 [PERSON_F]는 선실 문을 두드렸으나 응답을 받지 못했다. 그날 오후 늦게 [PERSON_F]는 [PRODUCT_A]에 올라 [PERSON_A]가 사망해 있고 [PERSON_B]가 간신히 숨을 쉬고 있는 것을 발견했다. [PERSON_F]는 두 차례 확인 당시 엔진이 작동하고 있지 않았다고 증언했으며, 이후 조사에서는 무색무취인 일산화탄소의 원인이 엔진이 아니라 [PRODUCT_B]인 것으로 확인되었다. [LOCATION_A]에서 [PRODUCT_A]로 하룻밤 외출을 하는 동안 일산화탄소 중독으로 [PERSON_A]는 사망했고 [PERSON_B]는 치명적인 부상을 입었다. [PERSON_A]와 [PERSON_B]가 입은 부상은 배기가스가 아니라 [PRODUCT_C]에 동력을 공급하던 [PRODUCT_B]에서 나온 무취·무미의 일산화탄소 가스로 인해 발생했다. 1981년에 이러한 유형의 [PRODUCT_A]가 판매될 때 일산화탄소 중독에 관한 두 가지 경고가 함께 제공되었다. 하나는 발전기 제조업체인 [ORGANIZATION_A]가 작성했고, 다른 하나는 [ORGANIZATION_B]가 작성했다. [COMPANY_A]는 구매자들에게 다른 설명서도 제공했다. 두 경고는 모두 주로 엔진 배기가스로 인한 일산화탄소 노출을 다루었다. [PERSON_A]와 [PERSON_E]가 [PRODUCT_A]를 구입할 당시, 판매점의 서비스 관리자 [PERSON_G]와 영업사원 [PERSON_H]는 배기가스와 일산화탄소, 그리고 위험한 가스를 제거하기 위해 [PRODUCT_A]를 환기해야 할 필요성에 대해 이들에게 경고했다. [PERSON_G]와 [PERSON_H]는 창문과 해치를 열어 공기가 통과하는 환기를 시연했고, 주 추진 엔진이 작동할 때는 뒷문을 열어 둬야 한다고 설명했으며, [PERSON_G]는 앞쪽 해치를 닫은 채 엔진을 공회전시키면 일산화탄소가 축적될 수 있다고 말했다. [PERSON_B], [PERSON_C], [PERSON_D]는 [PRODUCT_B]에서 일산화탄소가 안전하게 대기 중으로 배출되었지만 바람에 의해 [PRODUCT_A] 안으로 다시 불어 들어와 작은 틈을 통해 승객 선실에 유입되면서 "이동하는 일산화탄소"가 사건을 일으켰다고 주장했다. [COMPANY_A]의 전문가는 이러한 인과관계 설명에 동의했지만, 그 현상은 드물며 일산화탄소가 위험한 수준으로 축적되려면 승객 선실의 환기가 막혀 있어야 한다고 증언했다. 전문가는 세 가지 예방조치를 제시했다. 1981년에는 일산화탄소 감지 장치를 사용할 수 없었으므로 감시자를 배치하는 것, 바람의 흐름이 선미에서 멀어지는 방향으로 불도록 [PRODUCT_A]를 측면이 아니라 선수에서 계류하는 것, 또는 잠들기 전에 공기가 통과하는 환기를 만드는 것이었다. 전문가는 [COMPANY_A]의 설명서에 그러한 지침이나 경고가 전혀 포함되어 있지 않았다는 점을 인정했지만, 관련된 특정 [PRODUCT_A] 모델에서 그러한 유형의 사망을 초래한 사건은 보고된 적이 없다고 증언했다.

neutral_fact_en: [COMPANY_D], the predecessor of [COMPANY_B], entered into a construction management agreement with [COMPANY_A] under which [COMPANY_A] agreed to manage remaining construction of [PROPERTY_A]. Under the agreement, [COMPANY_A] was obligated to hire subcontractors and provide the work, labor, services, materials, supplies, and equipment necessary to complete the project. [COMPANY_A] later subcontracted with [COMPANY_C] for firestopping work on the project. Firestopping involved installing fire-retardant material around openings in walls to prevent smoke and fire from spreading between rooms. Under the subcontract, [COMPANY_C] was to install [PRODUCT_A] around certain electrical boxes, but the parties disputed whether [COMPANY_C] was required to install [PRODUCT_A] around the electrical boxes in the rooms' separation walls. The agreement contained a payment-related provision under which, through incorporation into the subcontract, [COMPANY_C]'s right to payment for its work was contingent upon [COMPANY_B]'s payments to [COMPANY_A]. The subcontract required [COMPANY_C] to provide firestop protection for electrical boxes where the boxes were required to have a minimum clear distance in rated walls or partitions. Trial testimony supported [COMPANY_C]'s contention that it believed the guest-room walls were not rated. Testimony also indicated that [COMPANY_A] instructed [COMPANY_C] to insulate according to room mockups used as examples for builders. The mockups did not contain [PRODUCT_A] on the electrical boxes in the rooms' separation walls, but a [COMPANY_A] official testified that he had never directed [COMPANY_C] to omit [PRODUCT_A] based on the mockups' omission of them. The subcontract required [COMPANY_C] to obtain written approval from [COMPANY_A] before deviating from its provisions, and [COMPANY_C] presented no evidence of written approval or a change order eliminating the [PRODUCT_A] requirement. After much of the work on the project was completed, [INSTITUTION_A] issued a correction notice stating that [PRODUCT_A] were required around the electrical boxes in the rooms' separation walls. Although [COMPANY_C] provided [COMPANY_A] with confirmation that it had installed [PRODUCT_A] in accordance with the subcontract, [COMPANY_A]'s subsequent inspection revealed that [PRODUCT_A] had not been installed in most of the rooms' separation walls, except for certain walls on the project's fifth and sixth floors. In an attempt to resolve the [PRODUCT_A] situation, [COMPANY_A] sent a letter to [COMPANY_B], acknowledging that [COMPANY_C] may have believed that [INSTITUTION_A] did not require [PRODUCT_A] in the rooms' separation walls above the 19th floor and explaining that [COMPANY_C]'s failure to install [PRODUCT_A] in those walls was likely a good-faith mistake. [COMPANY_A] directed [COMPANY_C] to retrofit all of the guest-room walls by installing the omitted [PRODUCT_A] according to [INSTITUTION_A] requirements. Retrofitting the walls required substantial work because most of the rooms had already been completed. [COMPANY_C]'s failure to install [PRODUCT_A] in the rooms' separation walls led [COMPANY_A] to direct [COMPANY_C] to retrofit the walls, and the retrofit required substantial work because most of the rooms had already been completed. [COMPANY_C] incurred labor costs of [CURRENCY_AMOUNT_A] associated with the retrofit. [COMPANY_A] incurred damages of [CURRENCY_AMOUNT_B] for the retrofit work. After the retrofit work was completed, [COMPANY_C] recorded a lien on the project for [CURRENCY_AMOUNT_C]. At trial, [COMPANY_A] and [COMPANY_C] made oral stipulations, excluding the [PRODUCT_A] issue, regarding the value and amount owed for certain approved change orders, pending change orders, and back charges.

neutral_fact_source: [COMPANY_D], the predecessor of [COMPANY_B], entered into a construction management agreement with [COMPANY_A] under which [COMPANY_A] agreed to manage remaining construction of [PROPERTY_A]. Under the subcontract, [COMPANY_C] was to install [PRODUCT_A] around certain electrical boxes, but the parties disputed whether [COMPANY_C] was required to install [PRODUCT_A] around the electrical boxes in the rooms' separation walls. The agreement contained a payment-related provision under which, through incorporation into the subcontract, [COMPANY_C]'s right to payment for its work was contingent upon [COMPANY_B]'s payments to [COMPANY_A]. The subcontract required [COMPANY_C] to provide firestop protection for electrical boxes where the boxes were required to have a minimum clear distance in rated walls or partitions. Trial testimony supported [COMPANY_C]'s contention that it believed the guest-room walls were not rated. Testimony also indicated that [COMPANY_A] instructed [COMPANY_C] to insulate according to room mockups used as examples for builders. The mockups did not contain [PRODUCT_A] on the electrical boxes in the rooms' separation walls, but a [COMPANY_A] official testified that he had never directed [COMPANY_C] to omit [PRODUCT_A] based on the mockups' omission of them. The subcontract required [COMPANY_C] to obtain written approval from [COMPANY_A] before deviating from its provisions, and [COMPANY_C] presented no evidence of written approval or a change order eliminating the [PRODUCT_A] requirement. neutral_fact_en: [COMPANY_A] manufactures various models of swimming pool filters, including [PRODUCT_A]. In 2006, [PERSON_A] purchased [PRODUCT_A] for use in a backyard swimming pool and integrated its canister into a preexisting filter system after a previous filter canister malfunctioned. [PERSON_A] connected the pool filter system to an automatic timer that could turn it off at night and on during the day. On July 1, 2008, after the system had been turned off, [PERSON_A] manually turned it on while anticipating the arrival of guests. When [PERSON_A] manually turned on the pool filter system, the canister exploded. Pieces from the exploding canister struck [PERSON_A]'s left eye and ruptured the eyeball, which was removed and replaced with a prosthesis. The explosion of the canister caused the injury to [PERSON_A]'s eye; the precise circumstances surrounding the injury were disputed, but this causal link was not disputed. [PERSON_A] alleged that [PRODUCT_A] lacked either a redundant or secondary restraint for the canister or an external automatic air-release valve for compressed air, and alleged that [COMPANY_A] failed to provide adequate warnings about the risk of explosion. [PRODUCT_A] had a split-shell design consisting of two pieces held together by a steel clamp, with removable filter grids inside; water was pumped through the grids under pressure to trap debris. When a residential pool filtration system was completely turned off, water stopped flowing and air could bleed into the system; residential systems were regularly turned on and off to save electricity. Testimony indicated that most residential pool owners used timers to turn their filter systems off at night and on during the day. When the system restarted, air that entered while it was off could be pushed into the canister and become trapped against clogged filter grids, allowing pressure to build inside the canister. If pressurized air could not escape, pressure could rise beyond the metal clamp's ability to hold the canister together, causing the canister to explode. When [PRODUCT_A] was connected to an automatic timer, the manual recommendation to bleed excess air each time the system cycled could not be followed without homeowner action. [PERSON_A] contended that known explosion risks made [PRODUCT_A] unsafe during normal operation. [COMPANY_A] countered that the explosion resulted from an explosive pressure condition that [PERSON_A] created through improper and unforeseeable misuse of the canister. [COMPANY_A] alleged that [PERSON_A] installed [PRODUCT_A] on an obsolete preexisting pool-filter system that was not designed for it and contained a positive shut-off valve whose misuse could increase the risk of pressure conditions and explosions. Two experts testified that pressure-related pool-filter explosions were known in the industry, that [PRODUCT_A]'s design was unsafe, and that safer alternatives with automatic external pressure-relief valves and redundant restraints existed. A company engineer testified that, between 1998 and 2008, [COMPANY_A] received no explosion claims involving split-shell canisters with automatic valves but received more than 50 reports involving split-shell models without those valves. He also testified that pressure conditions could accidentally arise through improper consumer cleaning or repeated cycling of the system. [COMPANY_A] contended that [PRODUCT_A] was safe and that [PERSON_A] caused the explosion by creating a pressure condition while improperly backwashing the system, then lied about how the explosion occurred. After the explosion and before trial, [PERSON_A] disposed of parts of the pool filtration system, including the separation tank, selector valve, shut-off valves, pipes, and plumbing. [PERSON_A] testified that the canister exploded spontaneously when he merely turned on the pool filter system while standing a short distance away. [COMPANY_A] argued that photographs of objects near the canister suggested [PERSON_A] was servicing the filter when it exploded, but [PERSON_A] disputed that contention. Medical records indicated that [PERSON_A] told a physician he had been servicing the filter, while he testified that he had never cleaned it and believed [COMPANY_B] performed that work. [PERSON_A]'s experts testified that their conclusion that the injury resulted from [PRODUCT_A]'s design depended on [PERSON_A]'s account of how the explosion occurred; they acknowledged that the conclusion might not remain valid if that account were shown to be false.
neutral_fact_ko: [COMPANY_A]는 [PRODUCT_A]를 포함한 다양한 모델의 수영장 필터를 제조한다. 2006년에 [PERSON_A]는 뒷마당 수영장에서 사용하기 위해 [PRODUCT_A]를 구입했고, 이전 필터 캐니스터가 고장 난 후 그 캐니스터를 기존 필터 시스템에 통합했다. [PERSON_A]는 수영장 필터 시스템을 밤에는 끄고 낮에는 켤 수 있는 자동 타이머에 연결했다. 2008년 7월 1일, 시스템이 꺼져 있던 후 [PERSON_A]는 손님들이 도착할 것을 예상하면서 수동으로 시스템을 켰다. [PERSON_A]가 수영장 필터 시스템을 수동으로 켰을 때 캐니스터가 폭발했다. 폭발한 캐니스터의 파편이 [PERSON_A]의 왼쪽 눈을 강타하여 안구가 파열되었고, 그 안구는 제거된 후 의안으로 대체되었다. 캐니스터의 폭발이 [PERSON_A]의 눈 부상을 초래했다. 부상을 둘러싼 정확한 상황은 다투어졌지만, 이러한 인과관계는 다투어지지 않았다. [PERSON_A]는 [PRODUCT_A]에 캐니스터를 위한 중복 또는 보조 고정장치나 압축공기를 위한 외부 자동 공기 배출 밸브가 없었다고 주장했으며, [COMPANY_A]가 폭발 위험에 관한 적절한 경고를 제공하지 않았다고 주장했다. [PRODUCT_A]는 강철 클램프로 함께 고정된 두 개의 부품으로 구성된 분할 셸 설계였고, 내부에는 탈착식 필터 그리드가 있었다. 잔해를 포집하기 위해 물은 압력을 받아 그리드를 통과해 펌핑되었다. 주거용 수영장 여과 시스템이 완전히 꺼지면 물의 흐름이 멈추고 공기가 시스템 안으로 유입될 수 있었다. 주거용 시스템은 전기를 절약하기 위해 정기적으로 켜지고 꺼졌다. 증언에 따르면 대부분의 주거용 수영장 소유자는 필터 시스템을 밤에는 끄고 낮에는 켜기 위해 타이머를 사용했다. 시스템이 재가동되면 꺼져 있는 동안 유입된 공기가 캐니스터 안으로 밀려 들어가 막힌 필터 그리드에 갇힐 수 있었고, 이에 따라 캐니스터 내부에 압력이 쌓일 수 있었다. 가압된 공기가 빠져나갈 수 없으면 압력이 금속 클램프가 캐니스터를 함께 고정할 수 있는 한계를 넘어 상승하여 캐니스터가 폭발할 수 있었다. [PRODUCT_A]가 자동 타이머에 연결되었을 때에는 시스템이 작동 주기를 거칠 때마다 과도한 공기를 배출하라는 수동 권고를 주택 소유자의 조치 없이는 따를 수 없었다. [PERSON_A]는 알려진 폭발 위험 때문에 [PRODUCT_A]가 정상 작동 중 안전하지 않았다고 주장했다. [COMPANY_A]는 그 폭발이 [PERSON_A]가 캐니스터를 부적절하고 예측할 수 없는 방식으로 오용하여 발생시킨 폭발성 압력 상태에서 비롯되었다고 반박했다. [COMPANY_A]는 [PERSON_A]가 [PRODUCT_A]용으로 설계되지 않은 구식 기존 수영장 필터 시스템에 [PRODUCT_A]를 설치했으며, 그 시스템에는 오용될 경우 압력 상태와 폭발의 위험을 증가시킬 수 있는 양정지 밸브가 포함되어 있었다고 주장했다. 두 명의 전문가는 압력과 관련된 수영장 필터 폭발이 업계에 알려져 있었고, [PRODUCT_A]의 설계가 안전하지 않았으며, 외부 자동 압력 방출 밸브와 중복 고정장치를 갖춘 더 안전한 대안이 존재했다고 증언했다. 회사 엔지니어는 1998년부터 2008년 사이에 [COMPANY_A]가 자동 밸브가 있는 분할 셸 캐니스터와 관련된 폭발 청구를 받지 않았지만, 그러한 밸브가 없는 분할 셸 모델과 관련된 보고는 50건 넘게 받았다고 증언했다. 그는 또한 소비자가 부적절하게 청소하거나 시스템을 반복적으로 작동 주기를 거치게 함으로써 압력 상태가 우발적으로 발생할 수 있다고 증언했다. [COMPANY_A]는 [PRODUCT_A]가 안전했으며 [PERSON_A]가 시스템을 부적절하게 역세척하는 동안 압력 상태를 만들어 폭발을 일으킨 후 폭발이 발생한 방식에 대해 거짓말했다고 주장했다. 폭발 후 재판 전에 [PERSON_A]는 분리 탱크, 선택 밸브, 차단 밸브, 파이프 및 배관을 포함한 수영장 여과 시스템의 일부를 폐기했다. [PERSON_A]는 짧은 거리만큼 떨어져 서서 단지 수영장 필터 시스템을 켰을 때 캐니스터가 저절로 폭발했다고 증언했다. [COMPANY_A]는 캐니스터 근처 물체들의 사진이 폭발 당시 [PERSON_A]가 필터를 정비하고 있었음을 시사한다고 주장했지만, [PERSON_A]는 그 주장을 다투었다. 의료 기록에는 [PERSON_A]가 의사에게 필터를 정비하고 있었다고 말했다고 기재되어 있었고, [PERSON_A]는 자신이 필터를 청소한 적이 전혀 없으며 [COMPANY_B]가 그 작업을 했다고 생각한다고 증언했다. [PERSON_A]의 전문가들은 부상이 [PRODUCT_A]의 설계에서 비롯되었다는 자신들의 결론이 폭발이 발생한 방식에 관한 [PERSON_A]의 설명에 의존했다고 증언했다. 그들은 그 설명이 거짓으로 밝혀질 경우 그 결론이 더 이상 유효하지 않을 수 있음을 인정했다.

When the system restarted, air that entered while it was off could be pushed into the canister and become trapped against clogged filter grids, allowing pressure to build inside the canister. If pressurized air could not escape, pressure could rise beyond the metal clamp's ability to hold the canister together, causing the canister to explode. When [PRODUCT_A] was connected to an automatic timer, the manual recommendation to bleed excess air each time the system cycled could not be followed without homeowner action. [PERSON_A] contended that known explosion risks made [PRODUCT_A] unsafe during normal operation. [COMPANY_A] countered that the explosion resulted from an explosive pressure condition that [PERSON_A] created through improper and unforeseeable misuse of the canister. [COMPANY_A] alleged that [PERSON_A] installed [PRODUCT_A] on an obsolete preexisting pool-filter system that was not designed for it and contained a positive shut-off valve whose misuse could increase the risk of pressure conditions and explosions. Two experts testified that pressure-related pool-filter explosions were known in the industry, that [PRODUCT_A]'s design was unsafe, and that safer alternatives with automatic external pressure-relief valves and redundant restraints existed. A company engineer testified that, between 1998 and 2008, [COMPANY_A] received no explosion claims involving split-shell canisters with automatic valves but received more than 50 reports involving split-shell models without those valves. He also testified that pressure conditions could accidentally arise through improper consumer cleaning or repeated cycling of the system. [COMPANY_A] contended that [PRODUCT_A] was safe and that [PERSON_A] caused the explosion by creating a pressure condition while improperly backwashing the system, then lied about how the explosion occurred. After the explosion and before trial, [PERSON_A] disposed of parts of the pool filtration system, including the separation tank, selector valve, shut-off valves, pipes, and plumbing. [PERSON_A] testified that the canister exploded spontaneously when he merely turned on the pool filter system while standing a short distance away. [COMPANY_A] argued that photographs of objects near the canister suggested [PERSON_A] was servicing the filter when it exploded, but [PERSON_A] disputed that contention. Medical records indicated that [PERSON_A] told a physician he had been servicing the filter, while he testified that he had never cleaned it and believed [COMPANY_B] performed that work. [PERSON_A]'s experts testified that their conclusion that the injury resulted from [PRODUCT_A]'s design depended on [PERSON_A]'s account of how the explosion occurred; they acknowledged that the conclusion might not remain valid if that account were shown to be false.

[ORGANIZATION_A] placed [PERSON_A] and his brothers with [PERSON_B] as a foster caregiver without providing her foster-parent training before the placement. [PERSON_B] sexually abused [PERSON_A] on a regular basis for several years. [PERSON_A] reported the sexual abuse to authorities in June 2014, when he was nineteen years old; [PERSON_B] was arrested and charged in August 2014. [PERSON_A] alleges that [ORGANIZATION_A] failed to adequately investigate the prospective foster home and regularly monitor it after placement, including after referrals about what was occurring in the home. [PERSON_A] alleges that the abuse caused him severe emotional trauma and psychological injuries. [PERSON_A] alleges that [ORGANIZATION_A]’s failure to perform its asserted placement and monitoring responsibilities resulted in his long-term sexual abuse, which in turn caused his severe emotional trauma and psychological injuries. [PERSON_A] stated that he did not tell anyone at [ORGANIZATION_A] about the sexual abuse because he feared that [ORGANIZATION_A] would separate him from his brothers if they were removed from [PERSON_B]’s home. [PERSON_A] alleges that [ORGANIZATION_A] responded to the home after several referrals but did nothing to protect him. neutral_fact_en: On July 14, 2011, [PERSON_A] was injured when [PERSON_A]’s vehicle collided with a truck owned by [COMPANY_A] and operated by [PERSON_B]. [PERSON_B] testified that he arrived at a jobsite at [LOCATION_A] to retrieve a [PRODUCT_A] being leased and utilized by [COMPANY_B]. He testified that stacks of bricks and vehicles blocked the main entrance, so he used a construction entrance, where the clearance was partially obstructed by the [PRODUCT_A] and a [VEHICLE_B]. [PERSON_B] stopped his truck while it protruded into the main roadway, exited it, and adjusted the truck’s axle to make a tighter turn into the jobsite and clear the [VEHICLE_B] and [PRODUCT_A]. When [PERSON_B] returned to his truck and continued pulling into the jobsite, [PERSON_A] collided with the truck and sustained serious injuries. The collision occurred after [PERSON_B] stopped his truck protruding into the main roadway and then returned to it to continue entering the jobsite. neutral_fact_en: In December 2010, [PERSON_A] and [PERSON_B], the paternal grandparents of [PERSON_C], were granted legal guardianship of [PERSON_C]. After the guardianship was granted, [PERSON_C] resided with [PERSON_A] and [PERSON_B] at [LOCATION_A]. The initial petition alleged that [PERSON_F] engaged in domestic violence in the presence of [PERSON_C]’s sister, failed to maintain the sister’s hygiene, and failed to provide the children with necessary food, clothing, supervision, and housing. As to [PERSON_C], the petition alleged that [PERSON_F] placed [PERSON_C] at risk of harm by failing to provide financial support during some periods of [PERSON_C]’s life. The address listed for [PERSON_C] was [PERSON_A] and [PERSON_B]’s address at [LOCATION_A]. The initial petition did not name [PERSON_A] and [PERSON_B] as respondents. On the same day, [INSTITUTION_A] entered an order temporarily committing the children to [ORGANIZATION_A]’s custody, but [PERSON_C] remained in [PERSON_A] and [PERSON_B]’s custody. Four days later, [ORGANIZATION_A] indicated that it intended to file an amended petition naming [PERSON_A] and [PERSON_B] as adult respondents. According to [PERSON_A] and [PERSON_B], [ORGANIZATION_A] personnel instructed them to appear at the hearing with [PERSON_C]. When they arrived, [ORGANIZATION_A] took [PERSON_C] into its physical custody pursuant to [INSTITUTION_A]’s orders transferring temporary custody to [ORGANIZATION_A]. On August 3, 2012, [ORGANIZATION_A] filed an amended petition identifying [PERSON_A] and [PERSON_B] as [PERSON_C]’s legal guardians and residents of [LOCATION_A]. [PERSON_A] and [PERSON_B] alleged that [ORGANIZATION_A] knew they had previously been granted legal guardianship of [PERSON_C] and nevertheless omitted them from the original petition or presented the allegations in a way that implied that [PERSON_C] lived in [PERSON_C]’s parents’ home. [PERSON_A] and [PERSON_B] alleged that, instead of providing notice of the proceedings, [ORGANIZATION_A] induced them to bring [PERSON_C] to the preliminary hearing so that [ORGANIZATION_A] could assume custody of [PERSON_C]. They also alleged that [ORGANIZATION_A] knew [PERSON_C] was being properly cared for in their home, based on reports from [ORGANIZATION_A] employees from 2010. Upon arriving for the hearing, [ORGANIZATION_A] took [PERSON_C] from [PERSON_A] and [PERSON_B]’s physical custody and placed [PERSON_C] in [ORGANIZATION_A]’s physical custody. [ORGANIZATION_A]’s physical custody of [PERSON_C] resulted from [INSTITUTION_A]’s orders transferring temporary custody to [ORGANIZATION_A]. Before taking physical custody of [PERSON_C], [ORGANIZATION_A] informed [PERSON_A] and [PERSON_B] about the issues arising from substantiated abuse and neglect claims concerning their home and informed them that it was taking [PERSON_C] into custody pursuant to [INSTITUTION_A]’s order. It is undisputed that [PERSON_A] and [PERSON_B] had actual notice of the proceedings, filed a verified answer to an amended petition, and appeared at and participated in hearings after being named as respondents.
neutral_fact_ko: 2010년 12월, [PERSON_C]의 친조부모인 [PERSON_A]와 [PERSON_B]에게 [PERSON_C]에 대한 법적 후견권이 부여되었다. 후견권이 부여된 후, [PERSON_C]는 [LOCATION_A]에서 [PERSON_A] 및 [PERSON_B]와 함께 거주했다. 최초 청원서는 [PERSON_F]가 [PERSON_C]의 자매가 있는 자리에서 가정폭력을 행사했고, 그 자매의 위생을 관리하지 않았으며, 아이들에게 필요한 음식, 의복, 감독 및 주거를 제공하지 않았다고 주장했다. [PERSON_C]에 관해서는, 청원서가 [PERSON_F]가 [PERSON_C]의 생애 중 일부 기간 동안 재정적 지원을 제공하지 않음으로써 [PERSON_C]를 해를 입을 위험에 처하게 했다고 주장했다. [PERSON_A]와 [PERSON_B]는 [ORGANIZATION_A]가 자신들에게 이전에 [PERSON_C]에 대한 법적 후견권이 부여되었다는 사실을 알고 있었음에도, 최초 청원서에서 자신들을 제외했거나 [PERSON_C]가 [PERSON_C]의 부모 집에 사는 것처럼 암시하는 방식으로 주장들을 제시했다고 주장했다. [PERSON_A]와 [PERSON_B]는 [ORGANIZATION_A]가 절차에 대한 통지를 제공하는 대신, [ORGANIZATION_A]가 [PERSON_C]의 보호를 맡을 수 있도록 자신들이 [PERSON_C]를 예비 심리에 데려오게 했다고 주장했다. 또한 그들은 [ORGANIZATION_A]가 2010년의 [ORGANIZATION_A] 직원들의 보고에 근거하여 [PERSON_C]가 자신들의 집에서 적절히 돌봄을 받고 있다는 사실을 알고 있었다고 주장했다. 심리에 도착하자, [ORGANIZATION_A]는 [PERSON_A]와 [PERSON_B]의 물리적 보호에서 [PERSON_C]를 데려가 [ORGANIZATION_A]의 물리적 보호 아래 두었다. [ORGANIZATION_A]가 [PERSON_C]를 물리적으로 보호하게 된 것은 임시 보호를 [ORGANIZATION_A]에 이전한 [INSTITUTION_A]의 명령들에 따른 결과였다. [PERSON_C]를 물리적으로 보호하기 전에, [ORGANIZATION_A]는 [PERSON_A]와 [PERSON_B]에게 그들의 집과 관련하여 입증된 학대 및 방임 주장으로부터 발생한 문제들을 알리고, [INSTITUTION_A]의 명령에 따라 [PERSON_C]를 보호하게 된다고 알렸다. [PERSON_A]와 [PERSON_B]가 절차에 대해 실제로 통지받았고, 수정 청원서에 대한 선서 인증 답변서를 제출했으며, 피청구인으로 지명된 후 심리에 출석하고 참여했다는 점은 다툼이 없다.

neutral_fact_en: [COMPANY_A] sold concrete and related items, delivered those products to customers, and employed [PERSON_B] as a truck driver. On August 28, 1999, [PERSON_B] was killed in a single-vehicle accident while delivering concrete during [COMPANY_A]'s business operations. [PERSON_B] died in the single-vehicle accident. [PERSON_A] alleged that [COMPANY_A]'s truck had become dangerously unsuitable for operation and that [COMPANY_A] had exposed [PERSON_B] to an unsafe working condition, which preceded [PERSON_B]'s fatal accident. [PERSON_A] alleged that [COMPANY_A] had not properly maintained the truck's brakes. After the accident, inspection found that one rear brake was completely inoperable and the other was critically deficient, and an investigation determined that both conditions existed when the fatal accident occurred. At the time of the accident, [COMPANY_A] had a commercial general liability policy through [COMPANY_B] and sought a defense from [COMPANY_B]. On October 4, 1999, [COMPANY_B] sent a letter to [PERSON_C], [COMPANY_A]'s president, acknowledging the claim and stating that it intended to defend subject to a reservation of rights. [PERSON_C] testified that he had read the terms and conditions of [COMPANY_A]'s coverage, but had not read the complete policy from cover to cover.
neutral_fact_ko: [COMPANY_A]는 콘크리트 및 관련 물품을 판매하고, 해당 제품을 고객에게 배송했으며, [PERSON_B]를 트럭 운전기사로 고용했다. 1999년 8월 28일, [PERSON_B]는 [COMPANY_A]의 영업 활동 중 콘크리트를 배송하다가 단일 차량 사고로 사망했다. [PERSON_B]는 단일 차량 사고로 사망했다. [PERSON_A]는 [COMPANY_A]의 트럭이 운행에 위험할 정도로 부적합해졌고, [COMPANY_A]가 [PERSON_B]를 안전하지 않은 작업 환경에 노출시켰으며, 그러한 상황이 [PERSON_B]의 치명적 사고에 앞서 발생했다고 주장했다. [PERSON_A]는 [COMPANY_A]가 트럭의 브레이크를 적절히 정비하지 않았다고 주장했다. 사고 후 검사에서 후방 브레이크 하나는 완전히 작동하지 않았고 다른 하나는 심각하게 불량한 상태였음이 확인되었으며, 조사 결과 사망 사고가 발생했을 때에도 두 상태가 모두 존재했던 것으로 밝혀졌다. 사고 당시 [COMPANY_A]는 [COMPANY_B]를 통해 상업 일반 배상책임 보험에 가입하고 있었으며, [COMPANY_B]에 방어를 요청했다. 1999년 10월 4일, [COMPANY_B]는 [COMPANY_A]의 사장인 [PERSON_C]에게 서한을 보내 해당 청구를 인정하고 권리 유보를 조건으로 방어할 의사가 있다고 밝혔다. [PERSON_C]는 [COMPANY_A]의 보장에 관한 약관과 조건을 읽었지만, 보험증권 전체를 표지부터 표지까지 완전히 읽지는 않았다고 증언했다.

Under [COMPANY_A]’s rental guidelines, [PERSON_A] did not qualify as an authorized additional driver because he lacked credit and proof of a permanent address; [PERSON_F] nevertheless gave [VEHICLE_C] to [PERSON_A] on March 13 or early the next morning to drive another man to a job opportunity.
